note: Structure instances placed by command. tools/place_town.py turns a settlement's entries into a datapack function (pads, /place template with rotation, jigsaw blocks replaced by their final state, donor loot removed, paths, waystone, world spawn), so a placement can be repeated exactly after a re-export. Positions are the minimum corner of each building's footprint after rotation; y comes from the terrain (the median ground under the footprint, levelled into a pad). Templates are the MIT CobblemonCityTowns donors copied under cobblers: (docs/world-building/STRUCTURE_CATALOG.md).

hometown.composition: A small coastal town on Pallet Meadows' upper bench. The main street runs north-south and leaves the town north as the first route toward gym 1; it crosses the east-west street at the Pallet sign's crossroads, the town centre. The Pokemon Center and Poke Mart face each other across the main street just north of the crossroads, where a returning trainer arrives. Five family houses line the cross street's western arm, on the lower ground that looks out over the sea. Oak's Lab stands apart on its own lane on the higher south-east corner. The waystone is beside the crossroads; players spawn on the main street south of the sign.
hometown.status: proposed: composition for a human to accept or rework in Axiom

waystone.unlock: not yet: placed unactivated; the flag-driven lock (EXP-020) is not wired for the hometown

hometown.built: placed and verified 2026-09-16 on the rescaled world; the composition itself is still a proposal for a human to accept or rework

plan.reading: From the hometown the route climbs onto the Viltri Plateau and enters from the south-west. The approach street rises gently NE straight into the plaza, so the Pokemon Center is the first building ahead (west side, door facing the plaza) and the Mart faces it across the square. The gym stands alone on the south-east knoll, the highest ground in town (y141-142): seen from the plaza over its lane, reached by climbing to it. The route leaves due north up the avenue toward Lake Viltri and Misty.

anchors.why: first building ahead of a player walking in from the hometown; its door opens onto the plaza
faces the Center across the plaza, so the two services read as a pair
anchors.rect_note: deepened by 2 on 2026-09-20: the CobbleTowns Mart is 23 deep once it faces the plaza, and the lot was 22. The street frontage is unchanged.

anchors.why: the knoll is the highest ground in town: a rock gym on the rock, visible from the plaza, reached up its own lane

waystone.note: flag gym1_cleared (data/progression.json); plaza north edge, on the way out

paving.why: a rock-gym town paved in worked stone: grey andesite streets, rough cobble lanes, a dressed-stone square. Spawn consequences, read from the loaded data: of 4,892 Cobblemon spawn entries only 17 need a base block (quartz in Nether quartz biomes, sand in beach biomes, concrete for Varoom and Revavroom in every overworld biome), and the Cobbleverse datapack repeats Varoom and Revavroom on all 16 concrete colours and adds Terapagos on amethyst in caves. So streets never use concrete. Stone, andesite, cobblestone, mud and prismarine carry no base-block spawn condition: wild Pokemon spawn on them as on any ground in the biome. Hostile mobs need block light 0, so the plan's lamps keep every street block within 14 blocks of a light. Note: the Pokemon Center and Mart donors have white and blue concrete in their roofs and walls, where Varoom can spawn in any town.
paving.lamp_why: a warm light set flush into the worked stone, like a lamp let into a mine floor; not a spawn condition in the loaded data

gym2_town.status: proposed: plan data for a human to compose from in Axiom. Built: street and plaza prep only; the waterfront gym lot is not levelled

plan.reading: The route comes down off the plateau along Lake Viltri's north shore and enters from the south-east with the water on the left. A shore street leads into the plaza; the Pokemon Center stands at its north-west corner facing the square and the Mart across the avenue. South of the plaza a short link reaches the lakeside promenade, and the gym stands on the waterfront between the two piers, facing the town with its back to the lake, so the water is the gym's backdrop and its arena can reach out over it. The route leaves due north up the avenue toward Surge.

anchors.why: on the plaza's north-west corner, its door toward the square a player crosses on arrival
across the avenue from the Center, on the way out north
anchors.rect_note: deepened by 2 on 2026-09-20: the CobbleTowns Mart is 23 deep once it faces the plaza, and the lot was 22. The street frontage is unchanged.

anchors.why: the town's reason to be here is the lake: the gym fronts the promenade and backs onto the water, its south edge at the shoreline
anchors.rect_note: deepened inland by 4 on 2026-09-20: cobbleverse:misty is 32 deep and the lot was 30. The south edge stays on the shoreline.

plan.reading: The climb from Lake Viltri tops out at the shelf's south-west corner, and the town appears sideways: a single walk running north along the lip with the whole flank falling away on the left. At the north end the walk opens into a belvedere, and that is where Mt Vessu's summit and Surge's signal array come into view together, up and to the right. From the belvedere a lane runs east along the foot of the wall to the gym, which is cut into the rock rather than standing on it. Nothing is more than one street from the drop.

plaza.why: the belvedere. Copper because the town is Surge's and because it will weather; it names no spawn condition in the loaded data.

anchors.why: off the belvedere's south-east corner, the first door on the right once the view has been had. The lentimas Centre carries bare podzol and dirt path, which is what this shelf is.

below the footprint at the top of the climb, on flat ground the pad still holds: the Mart is the first building reached, greeting the road before the town proper begins. Outside the footprint on purpose, so the shelf itself is left for houses

against the wall at the shelf's east end and cut into it: an electric gym should read as workings in the rock, not a hall on a lawn. Its door faces back down the lane, so the town is behind you when you go in.

house_lots.why: smaller and tighter than Brock's: there is no room to be generous on a shelf, and the cramped frontage is the point

waystone.note: flag gym3_cleared (data/progression.json); the belvedere's north edge, so it is the last thing passed on the way to the array path

paving.why: deepslate and tuff are the flank's own stone; the copper belvedere is the one deliberate colour in the town. None of the three is named by any spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json.

plan.prep_note: The pad is already pressed flat at y174.4 (data/sculpt.json), so the streets need almost no cut and fill; the work is the gym's bite into the wall east of x1730, which is the only real excavation in the town.

gym4_town.status: planned 2026-09-20; not laid out, not built

plan.reading: The road from the Trough comes in from the west and meets the garden before it meets a building: the plaza here is a green, not a square, and the streets run around it rather than through it. Every house faces the garden across a street. The Centre is on the green's west side, first door reached; the Mart is on the south. Erika's gym fronts the green from the north, glass to the south so the garden is what you see through it, and the lane from the green's west corner runs out to Peak Pond.

plaza.why: the green. Moss rather than stone, with the paving only where feet actually cross it, so the middle of the town is planting and not pavement. Moss names no spawn condition in the loaded data; the flowers that will go in it are already whitelisted in data/spawn_block_policy.json as garden planting.

anchors.why: on the green's west side, facing the road in: the first door a player reaches. The floaroma Centre comes with tulips and pink petals, which is the town this is.
on the ring's south side, its door to the green

fronting the green from the north with the whole garden in front of it. A grass gym should be looked into rather than entered from a street, and this is the only face of the ring with room for a wide building behind it.

house_lots.why: larger and further apart than either of the first two towns. The ground allows it, and a garden town should have gardens between the houses

waystone.note: flag gym4_cleared (data/progression.json); where the pond road meets the ring, on the green's west corner

paving.why: packed mud for the streets, the colour of a cart track rather than a pavement, and moss for the green itself. Neither is named by any spawn condition.

plan.prep_note: The site moves three metres across 179 blocks, so the streets need grading rather than cutting. The green should not be levelled flat: let it keep the fall it has, which is about a metre across its width.

gym5_town.status: approved 2026-09-21; laid out and audited on the disposable world 2026-09-21; not in the live world; no traders until the badge-gated stock lands

plan.reading: Route 5 comes down off the downs from the north-west and simply becomes the high street: there is no edge, the fields turn into yards and the yards into a town strung along the road. On the left the ground drops into a shallow fen; on the right it rises dry. Half-way along, the road opens into a market yard on the dry side. The gym is not on the road. You can see its roof over the reeds, but the way to it is a mangrove boardwalk that leaves the road behind the Centre, doubles back twice through the fen and arrives at a door facing away from town. A ninja's house should have to be found.

plaza.why: the market yard, on the dry side of the road where it bends. Mossy, because everything here is a little damp; moss names no spawn condition in the loaded data.

anchors.why: the first building on the high street, where the fields end; the fen boardwalk leaves the road just past it, so the Centre is also the landmark for finding the gym
anchors.rematerial: the coastal sand and podzol of its garden become mud and moss, its planting reeds and sugar cane: a Centre on a fen edge

anchors.why: on the dry side towards the far end of the street, the last shop before Route 6
anchors.rematerial: the same fen re-material as the Centre, so the pair belongs together

anchors.why: down in the fen, off the road, reached only by the boardwalk. Its door faces the boardwalk's end, away from the high street. Cobbleverse's own Koga.

house_lots.why: roomy yards along a road through fields, with a few cottages out on the boardwalk; the spacing is the opposite of Surge's shelf

waystone.note: flag gym5_cleared (data/progression.json); the market yard's north edge, on the dry side

paving.lamp_why: a sour green light for the poison town, set flush into the road; not a spawn condition
paving.why: packed mud and mangrove are the marsh's own materials; none of the three is named by a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json.

plan.prep_note: The road runs along the fen's edge at y116-118 and needs almost no cut; the boardwalk descends two or three blocks into the fen and is filled under, not dug. The gym lot is the one real levelling, in the fen at about y114.

plan.reading: Route 6 arrives from the west along the lakeshore flat and runs straight into a cross street, and at the crossing is the only true square in the region. From the square the whole town is visible at once: a white axis rising north up the slope, and at its head, looking straight back down it, the gym, with the observatory beside it on the high ground and the dojo across the gym street. The four blocks the axis and the cross street make are not houses. South-west is the market square, south-east the commons, and the Centre and the Mart face each other across the axis on the cross street. The houses stand in two rows along the outer streets, and at the lake end the department store closes the view. Route 7 leaves by the axis, down to the lake.

plaza.why: the square where the road meets the axis; the whole plan reads from here

anchors.why: west of the axis, opening onto the cross street beside the square, mirrored by the Mart
anchors.rematerial: its loose flower garden becomes a clipped parterre: box hedges of azalea leaves, white and pink tulips in beds, calcite paths

anchors.why: east of the axis, the Centre's mirror
anchors.rematerial: the same parterre re-material as the Centre

anchors.why: at the head of the axis on the highest ground, facing straight down it: visible from the square the moment you arrive. Cobbleverse's own Sabrina.

the south-west block, an open paved square off the cross street: the region's market. Its stalls are the traders, placed once the badge-gated stock lands; until then it is a square. Donor if a built market is wanted instead: bca:fighting/centers/center_the_farmers_market_fighting (48 by 49), which needs the block widened by six
the south-east block, left open: lawn, trees and a fountain (Cozy Home fountain blocks), the one green space in the region's biggest town and the view down to the lake
north-west of the axis on the high ground beside the gym: a psychic town's landmark, 16 by 16 and 23 tall. Mega Showdown's own, placed from the installed mod
beside the gym across the gym street's east end, as Kanto's Fighting Dojo stands next to Saffron's gym: BCA's battlepad centrepiece, 37 by 38, a trainers' arena
the lake end, east of the axis where Route 7 leaves: 40 by 72 and 41 tall, the region's one big city building, closing the view south from the square. BCA's, placed from the installed mod

house_lots.why: about thirty houses in two rows along the outer streets, so the inner blocks hold the market, the commons, the Centre, the Mart and the observatory. Sixty houses from about 29 designs repeated visibly and read as sprawl

waystone.note: flag gym6_cleared (data/progression.json); on the square, beside the axis

paving.lamp_why: a pale violet light for the psychic town, set flush into the paving; not a spawn condition
paving.why: white stone for a formal town; none of the three is named by a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (quartz, the obvious choice, is).

plan.prep_note: The flat takes the grid with little work; the axis climbs about four blocks over 150, graded to a steady rise. The gym lot at the top needs a small cut into the rise.

plan.reading: Route 7 comes over the lake crossing and up onto the rim from the north-east, and the cone fills the eastern sky. The town has put the mound between itself and the fire: its houses sit on the mound's lee, along lanes that follow the contour round it, and the road runs through an ash-black square at the mound's foot. East of the square nothing is built. A bare basalt causeway runs straight out across the open rim towards the cone, and at its end, alone, is the gym. You leave the town to get there.

plaza.why: the ash square at the mound's foot, where the road, the lee lane and the causeway meet

anchors.why: the first door off the road after the lake crossing, the game's first real barrier: you need it
anchors.rematerial: its basalt and deepslate kept, its garden's grass turned to coarse dirt and magma-coloured flowers (torchflowers, orange tulips): a Centre on a volcano

anchors.why: on the road out south-west, on the lee side
alone at the causeway's end on the open rim, between the town and the cone, facing back to the square. Outside the footprint on purpose. Cobbleverse's own Blaine.

house_lots.why: tucked in and tight: small houses close together on the mound's lee and along the road, none along the causeway

waystone.note: flag gym7_cleared (data/progression.json); the ash square's north-west corner

paving.lamp_why: an ember-orange light set flush into the black paving; not a spawn condition
paving.why: the volcano's own blacks. Magma block, the obvious floor for a fire town, is a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json and is not used.

plan.prep_note: The square and the road sit on the flat at y106-108. The lee lane climbs round the mound at two to four blocks above it and is cut to a contour. The causeway is level across the rim.

plan.reading: Route 8 arrives from the north-east at the foot of a broad, low dome, and the town lies up and behind it on the crown, its two lanes curving round the hill with the sea cliff somewhere beyond. The through street swings west along the town's northern foot, the side that looks out over the falling land towards the Rift, to a square where the town stops and Victory Road begins. Across that square stands the gym, and the road north runs past its door. Giovanni's gym is the gate: for seven badges it is the building everyone walks past, and for the eighth it is the one you have to go through to leave.

plaza.why: the gate square, where the town stops and Victory Road begins

anchors.why: the first door off the foot street after Route 8, the longest leg in the game
anchors.rematerial: its bare podzol and dirt path become coarse dirt, terracotta and dripstone: the ground-type town's earth

anchors.why: on the foot street below the crown lane, facing the square's approach: the last shop before Victory Road
anchors.rematerial: its sand and planting become coarse dirt and terracotta, as the Centre

anchors.why: across the gate square at the town's north-west corner, beside the road out: Victory Road runs past its door. Outside the footprint on purpose. Cobbleverse's own Giovanni.

house_lots.why: houses on the crown, facing out over the dome's falls; the foot street's north side stays open to the view

waystone.note: flag gym8_cleared (data/progression.json); the gate square, in front of the gym

paving.why: the ground-type town is paved in earth: granite on the through street, coarse dirt on the lanes, terracotta on the square. None is named by a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json.

plan.prep_note: The dome has only three or four blocks of relief inside the footprint, so the streets follow it with little cut; the gym's lot, below the square to the north-west, is levelled to the square.

plan.reading: Victory Road's last climb comes up the escarpment from the river valley and tops out at the plateau's east lip, onto a forecourt. The Centre and the Mart stand together on its north side, the last heal and the last shop, and the south side is left open to the drop and the view back down Victory Road. West of the forecourt a wide processional way crosses the plateau, lined with lamps and nothing else, straight to the League's door. Nobody lives here. It is a precinct, not a town, and it should feel emptied out for you.

plaza.why: the forecourt at the lip, where Victory Road ends

anchors.why: on the forecourt's north side: the last heal before the Elite Four
anchors.rematerial: its deepslate kept and its basalt turned to deepslate tiles and polished blackstone, to stand beside the League

anchors.why: beside the Centre on the north side, at the head of the processional way
Cobbleverse's own Kanto League, 111 by 120 and 159 tall, on the plateau's flat west half, its door at the end of the processional way. It reaches y277; the height pack allows y575.

house_lots.why: none: nobody lives at the League

waystone.note: proposed: opens with the League; on the forecourt, facing the processional way

paving.lamp_why: the League's cold light, flush along the processional way; the one lamp shared with another place (Misty's), since only five full-block lights exist that name no spawn condition
paving.why: deepslate tiles are the League building's own main block, so the way reads as its approach. None is named by a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json.

plan.prep_note: The forecourt and way are on the plateau's flat at y118-119, and the approach climbs two blocks from the lip. The League's lot is the real work: it spans y113 to y120, lowest at its west end outside the footprint, and is levelled to y118, cutting the east and filling up to five blocks on the west.
